title: pagerts
description: a TypeScript CLI that lists every link and resource a webpage references, as plain JSON.

content.heading: pagerts - the webpage resource extractor
content: **pagerts** fetches a URL (or reads a local HTML file) and prints every external resource it references - links, meta tags, scripts, styles - as JSON.
[https://github.com/akinevz2/pagerts](https://github.com/akinevz2/pagerts)

content.heading: what a webpage offers up
content: an HTML document advertises its dependencies in predictable places: the `

**pagerts** parses with JSDOM and inspects either the common resource-bearing tags or every element for selected link properties - the same dependency list [**graphbrowser**](/projects/graphbrowser) renders as a navigable graph.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: a commander/extra-typings CLI over a JSDOM parser. the build splits the executable entry (bin/main.js) from the library API (bin/lib.js) - tests import `run`, `runAll` and `printDryRun` without executing the CLI.
requires Node.js 20 or later; installs globally with `npm install --global pagerts`.

content.heading: usage
content:
```sh
$ npm install --global pagerts
$ pagerts https://example.com
```
**pagerts** all <urls...> - scan every element instead of the default tags
**pagerts** --dry-run <urls...> - preview the effective settings without fetching
**pagerts** --tags a,img - restrict extraction to specific tags
**pagerts** -p data-href - add link properties to search
**pagerts** --timeout 5000 - abort fetches that take longer than 5s
**pagerts** --no-json - the same report as a human-readable log

content.heading: quirks
content: a page that fails to load still gets an entry: `{"error": "Failed to load <url>: <reason>"}` - verbose on both channels, URL and reason included.
the default is no timeout - pass `--timeout <ms>` to abort slow fetches; the CLI exits promptly after printing either way (a timed-out fetch leaves no pending socket hanging).

content.heading: stable in v2.x
content: `--timeout <ms>` aborts each network fetch after the given number of milliseconds.
failures are verbose entries, not silent gaps - JSON and human-readable modes agree on the shape.
the CLI exits promptly after printing output; npm pack ships only the current build.
JSON is the default output; `--no-json` flips to the log form.

content.heading: examples
content: output is a JSON array with one entry per input URL: a `title`, the `url`, and a `resources` array of `tag` / `key` / `value` / `link` objects.
